intent: Slightly reduced lateral sensor spacing by shifting sensors inward by 0.01 m to test if a more concentrated sensor array improves line detection continuity through sharp turns on the slalom track. Retained the sixth center-front sensor and sensor size to maintain early detection benefits. Reduced kp to 6 previously to smooth control; now focusing on sensor layout fine-tuning to reduce line loss and steering oscillation. Expect improved line detection and control stability on slalom, maintaining strong oval and s-bend performance.
rationale: The previous iteration's adjustments—outward lateral sensor spacing by ±0.01 m, adding a sixth sensor at the center front (x=0, y=0.07), and reducing kp from 8 to 6—aimed to improve sharp turn coverage and control stability on the slalom track. Integration feedback confirms these changes improved line coverage and early detection on oval and s-bend tracks but slalom finish rates remain very low with high steering oscillation. To further address this, I will fine-tune sensor x-positions by shifting them slightly inward by 0.01 m (i.e., reduce lateral spacing) to test if a more concentrated sensor array improves line detection continuity through sharp turns. I will keep the sixth sensor at (0, 0.07) and maintain sensor size at 0.016 m and forward y-positions to preserve early detection benefits. The wheel track, radius, body size, and mass remain unchanged for stability. I expect this slight inward adjustment to improve line detection consistency on sharp turns, potentially reducing line loss events and steering oscillation on the slalom track, while maintaining strong performance on oval and s-bend tracks.
